DESCRIPTION: Gravelly soil - 50% orange, calcareous clayey soil cementing together 50% gravel and stone fragments, the latter consisting of highly angular quartz fragments 2-6mm diameter and slate fragments about 2mm in diameter. Slates - subangular, grey and fractured. Quartz and slate in equal proportions. Clay fraction increase to 80%, harder and more compact and colour changes from orange to buff to brown with depth.
Grit - well cemented indurated rock, 60% fine to medium grained moderately sorted, well rounded quartz. 40% rounded shale and other rock fragments, some lignitic. Probably carbonate cement.
Conglomerate - 70% shale and slate cobbles up to 3-4cm in diameter rounded. Some lignite. 30% highly angular quartz pebbles.

Calcareous metasiltstone - white moderately calcareous, powdery (marly?) clay containing 30% shale, slate and quartz fragments about 5mm in diameter. Coarse fraction increases to about 80% at 30m. Calcareous metasiltstone at about 50m becomes greyer and more compact with a higher clay content. Slightly calcareous. Near 57m coarse fraction decreases to 25%. 60m - buff mottled green, very hard stiff clay with about 5% grit. Slightly calcareous.
Shale - very fine grained shale with 20% clay (probably contamination from above). 10% of the shale possibly carbonaceous. Grey-green in colour.
